name: Render
summary: Render runs web apps, APIs, and background workers as always-on servers, deployed automatically from your Git repo.

free_plan_covers.note: Free web services get 750 instance hours a month but sleep after 15 minutes idle, and the free Hobby workspace now includes only 5 GB of bandwidth a month, enough for roughly 100 typical users.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Cheapest paid web service (Starter) is about $7/month for 512MB RAM and 0.5 CPU. Render's pricing page could not be read directly (script-rendered), so this is confirmed via third-party pricing trackers.

portability.note: Render runs a standard Docker image or native runtime with no proprietary APIs, so the app moves to any container host easily.

runtime_model.note: Web services run as always-on server processes (Docker or native runtime), not request-triggered functions.

persistent_disk.note: Persistent disks attach only to paid web services, private services, or workers, never free ones, and cost extra per GB.

long_lived_connections.note: Web services are regular always-on servers, so WebSocket connections work natively with no extra setup.

background_workers.note: Background Worker is a native service type that runs continuously without receiving web traffic, separate from the web service.

scheduled_jobs.note: Cron Job is a native Render service type for running code on a schedule.

free_plan_commercial_use.note: Render's docs say free instances should not be used for production applications, which effectively rules out a real commercial app.

framework_support.note: Next.js deploys as a full Node web service with SSR and API routes; static Vite apps and SvelteKit (Node adapter) both have official Render guides. Render runs Node.js, Python, Ruby and Go natively, so Express, Django, FastAPI, Rails and Go servers run as normal web services; Spring Boot, Laravel and ASP.NET Core run from a Docker image.

custom_domain_free.note: Render's free Hobby workspace plan includes 2 custom domains at no extra cost, and additional ones cost $0.25 per domain each month.

free_plan_sleeps.note: Render spins a free web service down after 15 minutes with no incoming traffic, and the next visitor waits about a minute while it wakes back up.

bandwidth_included.value: Hobby workspace (free): 5 GB a month, then $0.15 per GB. Starter ($7/month compute): still on the 5 GB Hobby workspace pool unless you also upgrade to the $25/month Pro workspace, which includes 25 GB.
bandwidth_included.note: Bandwidth is billed per workspace rather than per service, so the $7/month Starter compute plan alone does not raise your bandwidth allowance.

setup.step: Sign up at render.com and click New > Web Service.
Connect your Git repository; Render auto-detects the runtime or you set a build and start command.
Choose a plan (Free or Starter) and add environment variables under the Environment tab.
Click Create Web Service. Render builds and deploys, then redeploys automatically on every push.

builder_notes: Free web services sleep after 15 minutes of inactivity and take about a minute to wake up; do not use the free tier for anything users expect to load instantly.
The filesystem is ephemeral without a paid persistent disk ($0.25/GB/month); attach one for uploads or SQLite files that must survive redeploys.
Use the native Background Worker or Cron Job service types for anything that should not run inside the web service itself.
